capitals.name: Hetao (no fixed seat)
capitals.note: The page names no capital; the Xianyun are a steppe people of 'the Hetao ... to the upper Yellow River Valley': one dot in the Hetao for the map's label.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks the Xianyun). The page has no infobox or area. The shape follows its sentence on where they lived, 'an area that stretched from the Hetao (bend of the Yellow River) to the upper Yellow River Valley', with the lower Ordos named in the Duo You ding (c. 816). Soft, a people's range rather than a state.

region.text: 'an area that stretched from the Hetao (bend of the Yellow River) to the upper Yellow River Valley'

ledger.note: 840: the Xianyun first appear as attackers of the Zhou. The Duo You ding (840 BC) says 'the Xianyun greatly arose and broadly attacked Jingshi'; the page is silent on a founding date, and 'Written records place the first incursions against Zhou under the name Xirong (Western Rong) in 843 BC', so 840 is the first dated mention under their own name.

region.text: 'between the lower courses of the Jing (泾河) and Luo rivers and the Wei valley' (Book of Songs reference, undated), where King Xuan's campaigns of 823-815 are set

ledger.note: 823: the Xianyun attack again in King Xuan's fifth year. 'The Xianyun attacked again in 823 BC, the fifth year of reign of King Xuan'; King Xuan 'ordered a campaign against the Xianyun in the west' (Western Zhou page, which gives no year); the fighting is set 'in the vicinity of the capital Haojing'.

region.text: 'between the lower courses of the Jing (泾河) and Luo rivers and the Wei valley' (Book of Songs reference, undated), where King Xuan's campaigns of 823-815 are set

ledger.note: 815: the last dated Zhou campaign against them. The Buqi gui inscription (815 BC) records that 'The Xianyun broadly attacked Xiyu' and a campaign 'at Gaoyin'; the Guoji Zibai pan (816) says the Zhou 'attacked and conquered the Xianyun and reached the north of Luoshui'. The page gives no treaty or end of the fighting: 815 is the last dated clash.

region.text: 'an area that stretched from the Hetao (bend of the Yellow River) to the upper Yellow River Valley'

ledger.note: 771: the last dated mention of the Xianyun as a power. The page attributes the collapse of the Western Zhou in 771 to 'pressure from the Xianyun or the Quanrong' with uncertainty, and gives no end to the people; later annalists equated the name with the Xiongnu (Han) and the identification is disputed.

wars.name: Zhou campaigns against the Xianyun

zones.text: 'between the lower courses of the Jing (泾河) and Luo rivers and the Wei valley' (Book of Songs reference, undated), where King Xuan's campaigns of 823-815 are set

wars.outcome: Xianyun raids on the Zhou capital region (823, c. 816 at a Jing garrison in the lower Ordos, 815) answered by Zhou campaigns that, on the inscriptions, reached 'the north of Luoshui'; no border change is recorded.
wars.note: The page also dates raids in 843 (as Xirong) and 840 and 'c. 899-886' captured bronzes; the earlier ones are in the page's prose, not in the zone.

certainty.note: A steppe people with no stated boundary; soft throughout.

sources.title: Xianyun
sources.note: Range 'from the Hetao ... to the upper Yellow River Valley'; dated bronze inscriptions 840, 823, c. 816, 815; 771 collapse attributed to Xianyun or Quanrong; no infobox, founding or end.

notes: Pages opened (2 of up to 5): Xianyun, Western Zhou. Wikidata id left null (unreachable). WHAT THIS IS: the Xianyun as a people with a range, not a state with a border; FAMILY steppe. START -840 is the Duo You ding's date for the name Xianyun and END -771 the page's last mention as a possible cause of the Western Zhou's fall; neither is a founding or dissolution ('page silent'), both at confidence 1. REGION: the Hetao plus Ningxia is the researcher's reading of 'from the Hetao to the upper Yellow River Valley'; the page names no modern province for it. The Western Zhou page dates King Xuan's reign 827-782 and gives no BC year for his fifth-year campaign; 823 is the Xianyun page's figure. The Xianyun = Xiongnu identification, and Xianyun = Quanrong, are disputed on the page and not decided here. AREA: none.
